tip: Keşke plus a -se verb voices a wish: dinse (din + se) = if only it would stop.
-le on a noun means by or with: otobüsle (otobüs + le) = by bus, no separate word needed.
Insert -ebil for can or be able to: gidebilirim (git + ebil + irim) = I can go.
-ma plus a possessive makes a that-clause noun: varmamız (var + ma + mız) = our arriving, that we arrive.
Position words take genitive on the noun: köprünün altından (köprü + nün, alt + ından) = from under the bridge.
-erek says by doing something: yürüyerek (yürü + yerek) = by walking, describing how you go.
-malı means must or have to: hazırlamalıyız (hazırla + malı + yız) = we must prepare.
After a number the noun stays singular: altı sandalye = six chairs, sandalye not sandalyeler.
-dik plus a possessive makes a which-clause: gezdiğimiz yerler (gez + diğimiz) = the places that we visited.
Add -ın for a polite or plural command: kapatın = close (formal), versus plain kapat to one friend.
-ince means when or as soon as: gelince (gel + ince), so Bahar gelince = once spring comes.
hem ... hem frames both ... and: hem sağlıklı hem ekonomik = both healthy and economical.
Meğer plus a -miş verb marks a fact you just realized: gitmiş = turns out he had gone, not eyewitnessed.
-irdi marks a past habit, used to: giderdik (git + er + di + k) = we used to go, yüzerdik = we used to swim.
Umarım, I hope, is followed by the aorist here: iyileşirsin (iyileş + ir + sin) = you get better.
rağmen, despite, needs the noun in dative: Başarısızlığa rağmen (başarısızlık + a) = despite failure.
-alım means let's: başlayalım (başla + yalım) = let's start, the we-form suggestion ending.
göre takes the dative and means according to: Bana göre = in my opinion, bana being the dative of ben.
-mış olmalı means must have or probably has: bitmiş olmalı = the battery must have died, a guess from evidence.
-ip links verbs sharing one subject; only the last carries tense: oturup dinlenmek = to sit and rest.
For an action still going, put -dır on the time span plus present tense: Yıllardır ... yaşıyorum = I have lived here for years.
-di is what you saw, -miş what you only heard: oynadı = performed (seen), alkışlamış = apparently applauded (reported).
